about: Why an attack with no spec stays unvalidated: a person's note, read by tools/admission/manifest.py into the manifest's 'why' column. It never changes a class (manifest.py refuses an entry for an attack that has a spec or a stamp: the gate decides those). Written 2026-11-12 from local sandbox runs on vault-a and the one-flaw mutants (the runs are in the admission-2 branch evidence, evidence/admission-2-survey-2026-11-12/README.md).

reasons.race-ordering-unprovable: the attack has a race step; the gate counts a race only when per-receipt block heights show the calls overlapped, and the stored admission runs were made before the harness recorded them (steps[].receipts). At most partially validated until they are re-run
reasons.stopped-by-access-key: NEAR itself rejects the call before any guard code runs: the agent's key may call only pay on the guard (harness/src/setup.rs, AGENT_METHODS). No guard flaw can make it break
reasons.intent-only: every pay it makes is inside the policy (valid invoices, under the cap). Its oracle is what the owner intended (against_intent), which this gate version does not decide
reasons.no-one-flaw-finds-it: every pay is refused or valid on vault-a, and no single planted flaw makes it pay beyond the policy (measured where stated)
reasons.tests-another-contract: the calls go to NEAR Intents directly, not through the guard: what it tests is Intents' own access rules
reasons.not-an-attack-file: a prompt-injection scenario in tools/injection/scenarios.json, run by an agent, not a file of steps; the gate admits step files only
reasons.race-not-what-is-tested: a race attack whose spec checked one outcome, and the flaw it matched (M3: cap checked per payment; or M1: no payee check) breaks it whether or not the calls overlap. Even with ordering shown it would not validate the race, so its spec was withdrawn. Its gate run (partially validated) is kept in evidence/admission/<id>/
